gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Minn Kota's on-board Precision chargers (the PCL line; the older Digital and PC models are obsolete) charge 12V LiFePO4 at no more than 14.5 V, that Minn Kota tells owners to check that ceiling against the battery maker's charge spec, and that these chargers do not work with a single 24V or 36V lithium battery, so a 24V or 36V trolling setup has to use 12V Group 24 batteries wired in series, one charger bank per battery.
standout_why: I compared against all seven ChatGPT answers and the result list. On charging, every answer only says to 'use a LiFePO4-compatible charger' or check that the charger supports LiFePO4. None names a trolling-motor maker's on-board charger, its 14.5 V ceiling, or the exclusion of single 24V/36V lithium batteries. I could not open the rival pages themselves to check them line by line. solargenadvisor.com failed with a certificate error. vatrerpower.com returned 403. redodopower.com, wattcycle.com, renogy.com and litime.com returned 429. ipowerqueen.com failed with a certificate error, and Walmart showed a bot wall. The score therefore rests on what ChatGPT pulled from those pages, not on reading them in full.
decides: This finding does not change the pick. It adds a compatibility check the page can make the deciding check: a shopper who already has a Minn Kota PCL on-board charger should pick the battery whose maker-stated charge voltage works with a 14.5 V maximum. A 24V or 36V motor owner should buy two or three identical 12V Group 24 batteries for a multi-bank PCL charger, not a single 24V or 36V lithium battery. I could not open any candidate's charge-voltage spec from the maker, so the battery side of this check is still missing (see unsourced).

findings.label: Which Minn Kota chargers charge 12V LiFePO4
findings.source_title: Charging Lithium Batteries – Minn Kota Help Center (updated 2025-07-01)
findings.note: Quote: '12V lithium-based (LiFePO4) batteries can be charged with Minn Kota Digital (Obsolete), PC (Obsolete) or PCL chargers.'

findings.label: Maximum charge voltage and maker check
findings.source_title: Charging Lithium Batteries – Minn Kota Help Center (updated 2025-07-01)
findings.note: Quote: 'important to ensure our Max voltage of 14.5V meets the specifications of the Battery Manufacturer.' The same article says that where a charger has no lithium setting, battery makers may recommend the AGM setting.

findings.label: Exclusion: single 24V/36V lithium batteries
findings.value: Not compatible with single 24V and 36V lithium batteries
findings.source_title: Precision Charger Lithium (PCL) Features, Specifications and Manuals (2021-present) – Minn Kota Help Center
findings.note: Quote: 'The Minn Kota Chargers are not compatible with single 24V and 36V Lithium Batteries.' The PCL line is described as 'optimized for 12 volt lithium (LiFePO4) batteries'. Charging is per bank, for example 3 banks × 10 A on the MK 330PCL. So a 24V motor needs two 12V batteries in series on a 2-bank charger, and a 36V motor needs three on a 3-bank charger.

findings.label: Waking a battery from BMS standby
findings.value: PCL Auto Start tries to restart a lithium battery in BMS standby a set number of times
findings.source_title: Charging Lithium Batteries – Minn Kota Help Center (updated 2025-07-01)
findings.note: The article also warns that 'Most lithium batteries require that you remove all electrical connections to the battery before it will turn back on', and that in lithium mode the charger does not show state of charge well. The battery's Bluetooth app is then the only reliable state-of-charge readout.
